source.author: ov
source.text: At proceres, quoniam muros intrare vetaris, ruris honorati tantum tibi, Cipe, dedere, quantum depresso subiectis bubus aratro complecti posses ad finem lucis ab ortu, cornuaque aeratis miram referentia formam postibus insculpunt, longum mansura per aevum.
source.text_original: At proceres, quoniam muros intrare vetaris, / ruris honorati tantum tibi, Cipe, dedere, / quantum depresso subiectis bubus aratro / complecti posses ad finem lucis ab ortu, / cornuaque aeratis miram referentia formam / postibus insculpunt, longum mansura per aevum.
source.text_english: But the nobles, since you are forbidden to enter the walls, gave you, Cipe, only as much of the honored countryside as you could embrace from sunrise to sunset with the plow under oxen pressing the furrow, and they carved horns on the bronze posts, mirroring a wondrous shape, to remain for a long age.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hic soror Aeoliden aevum mansura per omne deserit, heu saevae nequiquam erepta novercae.
reuse.text_original: hic soror Aeoliden aevum mansura per omne / deserit, heu saevae nequiquam erepta novercae.
reuse.text_english: Here the sister leaves the Aeolid, to remain through all time, alas, snatched in vain from her cruel stepmother.
